aiOverview.content: In NREL's System Advisor Model (SAM), the State of Charge (SOC) parameters for a behind-the-meter (BTM) battery model manage how energy storage operates, bounds its capacity, and sets starting conditions.Minimum State of Charge (%):The lower boundary of the battery's operating window.The default value is typically 15% for most Li-ion battery types.SAM prevents the dispatch algorithm from discharging the battery below this percentage, preserving a reserve and protecting battery health.Maximum State of Charge (%):The upper boundary of the battery's operating window.The default value is typically 95% for most Li-ion battery types.SAM stops charging the battery once it reaches this level (unless specific grid or PV override rules apply).Initial State of Charge (%):The starting charge percentage of the battery at the very beginning of the simulation (Hour 0, Step 1).It dictates how much energy is immediately available before the first dispatch or charge cycle occurs.Dispatch Strategies (Behind-the-Meter):SAM controls BTM battery timing and power via heuristic or optimization dispatch modes, including:Manual dispatch: Time-based, user-specified charge and discharge schedules.Peak shaving dispatch: Automated control that discharges the battery to reduce demand charges based on forecasted load and PV generation.Price signals dispatch: Dispatches the battery based on time-of-use (TOU) or real-time electricity pricing tariffs.Look-ahead / Look-behind options: Uses perfect prediction or 24-hour historical data to optimize charging and discharging against PV and prices.You can review more detailed input definitions directly on the SAM Battery Dispatch BTM Help Page or the SAM Battery Storage BTM Overview.You can review more detailed input aiOverview.content: NREL Technical Report NREL/TP-6A20-64641, published in September 2015, is titled "Technoeconomic Modeling of Battery Energy Storage in SAM".Core Focus: This report details the integration of comprehensive lead-acid and lithium-ion battery performance and economic models into NREL's System Advisor Model (SAM).System Applications: It evaluates behind-the-meter (BTM) storage systems—such as residential, commercial, and third-party ownership configurations—aimed at utility bill reduction via energy arbitrage and demand charge management.Battery Chemistries Supported: The original framework introduced modeling capabilities for lead-acid and lithium-ion battery technologies, with later SAM versions expanding to flow batteries.Performance & Degradation Modeling: The report outlines how SAM handles terminal voltage, battery capacity, temperature effects, and detailed degradation mechanics to track physical wear and schedule battery replacements.Dispatch Control Options: It covers initial dispatch controllers that allowed users to program manual schedules or basic target-based routines to manage charging and discharging relative to photovoltaic (PV) generation and utility rate structures. (Note: More advanced automated look-ahead and peak-shaving dispatch algorithms were added in subsequent NREL reports like NREL/TP-5B10-).If you are looking for specific equations, degradation parameters, or download access to the full text, let me know which section of NREL/TP-6A20-64641 you need help with.If you are looking for specific equations, degradation parameters, or download access to the full text, let me know which section of NREL/TP-6A20-64641 you need help with.AI responses may include mistakes.
